lessons.title: Example: The placeholder attribute
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display Favorite as a hint in the input element by setting the placeholder.

Make sure to pick placeholder followed by = and then ", Favorite, ".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Display Favorite as a hint in the first input element, while leaving the other two hints unchanged.

Make sure to pick placeholder, followed by =, ", Favorite, and finally ".

lessons.title: Question: Different types of input
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

There's a space missing between input and typeThe input element is missing its closing tagNothing's wrong with this codeThe code doesn't have a br element

There's a space missing between input and type.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A browser reads <inputtype="range">. Why will it not create the intended range input?

Without a space, inputtype is read as the element name.A range input requires a closing </input> tag.The type attribute must come before the input element.The value range must be outside quotation marks.

Without a space, inputtype is read as the element name.

lessons.title: Question: The default type value
lessons.interactiveContent:
By default, what is the type of this input element if it is not defined? This is a great opportunity to research!

textpassworddatecolor

Make sure to pick text.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Someone enters a name in this input without adding a type attribute. Which control will the browser show?

A one-line text field.A hidden password field.A date picker.A color picker.

A one-line text field.

lessons.title: Question: Input layout
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display?

Two input elements on top of each otherTwo input elements next to each otherOne input element on top of a button elementThree input elements

Two input elements on top of each other.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A visitor types a first name, then moves to the next field. Which code element forces the second input onto a new line?

The <br> between the inputs.The second input's placeholder attribute.The two separate <input> tags by themselves.The question in the <p> element.

The <br> between the inputs.

lessons.title: Example: The type attribute
lessons.interactiveContent:
Hide the text the user types in by setting the correct attribute to password.

Make sure to pick type.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Hide the characters typed into the answer field while keeping the Answer hint.

Make sure to pick type, followed by =, ", password, and finally ".

lessons.title: Question: Highlighting groups
lessons.interactiveContent:
What would we use to group the elements in each of the two sections below?

A div elementA body elementAn img elementA p element

A div element.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What would we use to group the elements in each of the two sections below?

Which choice lets you style each section as one group?

Wrap the elements in each area in a div element.Put a separate body element around each area.Replace each area with one p element.Use an img element to contain each area.

Wrap the elements in each area in a div element.

lessons.title: Question: Nesting elements
lessons.interactiveContent:
How many elements are nested inside the div element on this page?

ThreeTwoFiveZero

Make sure to pick Three.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If you apply a style to this div, which three direct child elements are grouped by it?

The h4 and both p elements.Only the h4, because it appears first.The div and the h4 only.The text inside the paragraphs, but not the paragraphs.

The h4 and both p elements.

lessons.title: Example: The div element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Place a heading for Top Destinations in the first group of elements and a heading for Other Destinations in the second.

Make sure to pick h1 followed by /h1 and then h4, /h4.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Give Top Destinations the largest heading level and Other Destinations level four.

Make sure to pick h1, followed by /h1, h4, and finally /h4.

lessons.title: Example: Highlighting groups
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a group of elements for the website's title and a group of elements for a post using the div element.

Make sure to pick div, followed by div, and finally div.

lessons.title: Question: Nesting elements
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the element inside the div element called?

A nested h4 elementA nested p elementAn indented h3 elementA grouped h4 element

A nested h4 element.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In the shown structure, which element is the parent of the h4 heading?

The div element.The body element, because it contains every page element.The heading's text, because it is inside the h4.There is no parent because h4 is indented.

The div element.

lessons.title: Question 7
lessons.interactiveContent:
In between which tags should we place a link to make it a clickable list item?

Between <li> and </li>Between <ol> and <ol>Between <ul> and </ul>

Between <li> and </li>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A navigation link must appear as one item in a list. Which pair of tags should wrap that link?

Between <li> and </li>Between <ol> and <ol>Between <ul> and </ul>Between <a> and </a>

Between <li> and </li>.

lessons.title: *Question 8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display?

A list of linksA normal listThree links in a paragraphTwo links

A list of links.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A screen reader reaches the ul in this code. What kind of collection does it announce before the three destinations?

An unordered list with three linked items.A paragraph containing three links.Three headings followed by a list.An ordered list numbered one through three.

An unordered list with three linked items.

lessons.title: Question 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What can we add as a list item inside a list?

Links, images, lists, and textOnly text and other listsOnly text

Links, images, lists, and text.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You are building a list item for a menu that may include text, a link, or an image. Which description covers what a list item can contain?

Links, images, lists, and textOnly text and other listsOnly textOnly links

Links, images, lists, and text.

lessons.title: Example 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct tags to create an ordered list.

Make sure to pick <ol>, followed by </ol>.

lessons.title: Example 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the closing tags for <a> and <li>.

Make sure to type </a></li>.

lessons.title: Question: Webpage
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's a webpage?

A file with .html at the endA file with .png at the endA collection of files with .html at the end

A file with .html at the end.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A file named news.html is one page in a site. Which description best identifies that file?

A file with .html at the endA file with .png at the endA collection of files with .html at the endA file with .css at the end

A file with .html at the end.

lessons.title: Question: Files
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the file name usually given to a website's homepage?

index.htmlabout.htmlhomepage.htmlcontact.html

Make sure to pick index.html.

lessons.title: Question: Navigation
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display?

Three links on the same line followed by an image on a different lineThree links on different lines followed by an image on a different lineFour links on the same lineThree links on the same line

Three links on the same line followed by an image on a different line.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Before the image loads, where will it begin relative to the three navigation links?

On a new line after the links, because of <br>.On the same line after About, because images are inline by default.On a new line after each individual link.Before the links, because the image source starts with a slash.

On a new line after the links, because of <br>.

lessons.title: Example: Files
lessons.interactiveContent:
Link to stocks.html by coding /stocks.html.

Make sure to type /stocks.html.

lessons.title: Question: Naming convention
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we add a space instead of a hyphen in link?

The link doesn't workThe link works just fineThe webpage opens both pop.html and quiz.htmlAn error appears

The link doesn't work.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The link points to /pop quiz.html, and a file with that exact name exists. What happens when a visitor selects the link?

The browser opens that file, because the path matches its name.The browser looks for pop-quiz.html instead.The browser opens both pop.html and quiz.html.The browser refuses the link because filenames cannot contain spaces.

The browser opens that file, because the path matches its name.
